chunks: And from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A believer's dream is a part of seventy parts of prophethood, and amongst them are some who have been given one-third.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of a believer's dream in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the believer's dream as a fragment of prophethood (nubuwwah), reflecting the concept of 'minor prophethood' where divine inspiration continues in the faithful after the Prophet. While the general share is one-seventieth, the narration highlights a hierarchy of spiritual perception, noting that some believers receive a more substantial portion, specifically one-third, underscoring the varying degrees of insight (kashf) among the pious.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 71. It has been reported that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:
A believer's dream is a part of seventy parts of prophethood. And amongst them are some who have been given one-third.
